metadata.description: Stride task management skills for AI agents

plugins.name: stride
plugins.description: Drive the full Stride kanban task lifecycle from Claude Code — claiming, completing, creating and enriching tasks and goals, workflow orchestration, subagent dispatch, and automatic lifecycle hook execution, with optional gated integrations for exploratory manual testing, hardening findings into drafted regression checks, and deep security-considerations review. New in v1.62.0: the orchestrator skill is 42% smaller — 139,972 to 80,523 bytes — with gated and cold content moved into sibling reference files loaded on demand, never deleted. Step 5.5 (exploratory testing) and Step 5.6 (hardening) each keep their gate, Decision Summary and an explicit load instruction inline while their bodies move to optional-exploratory-testing.md and optional-hardening.md; every non-Claude-Code branch is consolidated into platform-other.md, loaded once at Platform Detection rather than sitting resident on the Claude Code path; and six cold lookup sections (the flowchart, Quick Reference Card, Platform Summary, Edge Cases, Failure Modes, and the workflow_steps name vocabulary) move to reference.md. Each extraction was proved lossless by reconstructing the pre-change file from its parts and diffing byte-for-byte against git. The release's most consequential change is not a size reduction: Step 7's worked reviewer_result example had fallen behind the contract it illustrated, listing five keys where the server's ReviewContract requires eight structured sections on any dispatched review and CompletionResultGate rejects on them unconditionally regardless of the grace flag — so an agent building its payload from that example was getting a hard 422. It is now a handoff to the canonical stride-completing-tasks schema rather than a corrected example, since a rewritten example would be a third copy with nothing keeping it in sync. Step 5's reviewer dispatch also gains a specified diff-derivation (it previously left the method to improvisation, most naturally a bare git diff that silently omits staged hunks and untracked files and returns nothing inside a nested subrepo) plus the data-not-instructions framing and redaction rules that were absent from it. Ships docs/token-baseline.md, a reproducible per-task token measurement taken from real transcript usage records rather than estimated from byte sizes. Known limitation, stated plainly: the goal's headline target of under 40KB is not met and is not reachable by extraction — the largest remaining section is Step 5 at ~20.8KB of hot-path procedure, and closing the gap would mean deleting rules.

plugins.name: stride-security-review
plugins.description: AI-powered security review via /stride-security-review:security-review. Two scan modes: diff (default, PR-gating) and --full (codebase posture check, batched with cross-batch dedup and skipped-files reporting). Detects 10 universal vulnerability classes plus 5 MAESTRO-derived agentic-AI classes (prompt injection, tool abuse, agent trust boundary, model output execution, vector-store poisoning). Seven framework rule packs (new in 2.3.0): Android/Kotlin (exported components, WebView JS bridge RCE, cleartext traffic, SharedPreferences credentials, SQLite injection, trust-all SSL), Django/Python (mark_safe, raw/extra SQL, CSRF, production settings, mass-assignment, open-redirect, deserialization, SSRF, DRF mass-assignment), Express/Node.js (reflected XSS, eval RCE, child_process injection, Mongoose NoSQL injection, prototype pollution), iOS/Swift (UserDefaults credentials, WKWebView file access, ATS arbitrary loads, URLSession trust-all, deep-link missing auth), Phoenix/Elixir (raw/1, force_ssl, CSRF, fragment interpolation, LiveView scope, mass-assignment, Token replay, System.cmd shell, LiveView upload guards, open-redirect), Rails/Ruby (html_safe, find_by_sql, CSRF, params.permit!, eval/send, open-redirect, deserialization, connection.execute, missing-auth, JSON-leak), React/Next.js (dangerouslySetInnerHTML, API route missing auth, redirect open-redirect, javascript: href scheme, getServerSideProps secret leak). Plus a multi-platform CI/CD pipeline pack (8 platforms) and a framework-agnostic Web defense-in-depth pack covering security headers (CSP/HSTS/X-Frame-Options/cookie flags). Every finding carries CWE-ID and OWASP Top 10 references. Opt-in flags: --maestro (7-layer threat classification with explicit non-AI mapping), --rci [N] (recursive criticism passes), --baseline (suppress acknowledged findings), --patches (surgical-fix unified diffs), --fail-on <severity> (CI exit-code gate), --base <ref> (PR-against-base diff scope), --sarif (SARIF v2.1.0 output for GitHub Code Scanning), --considerations <source> (considerations mode, new in 2.5.0 — verifies a task's security_considerations were actually mitigated by the diff via a per-consideration mitigated/partial/unmitigated verdict, byte-identical output when not set). Ships a reference GitHub Actions workflow and a TAP 13 eval runner over 72 fixtures with positive-and-negative-control coverage (including considerations-mode controls), plus golden-file tests for the deterministic SARIF/dedup/fingerprint/fail-on transforms (new in 2.4.0). Semantic analysis, not pattern matching. Loosely based on anthropics/claude-code-security-review.

plugins.name: stride-ideation
plugins.description: Turn a fuzzy idea into shipped Stride tasks via two slash commands — /ideate drives an interactive, profile-aware question loop that hard-gates seven requirements sections into a committed markdown doc, and /stridify decomposes that doc into Stride goals and tasks via the batch API.

plugins.name: stride-lite
plugins.description: Lightweight companion plugin to Stride — produces Stride-shaped goal and task markdown documents on disk from a free-text prompt plus an optional requirements directory. No API calls, no kanban setup, no auth files. Just markdown. Useful when you want the Stride field discipline (acceptance criteria, key files, pitfalls, testing strategy, dependencies) without committing to the full Stride server workflow — the documents it produces can be reviewed, edited, or later submitted to a real Stride deployment by hand or by tooling, but this plugin never does so itself. Surface: three slash commands and one workflow skill. /stride-lite:create-goal decomposes a prompt into a goal directory with one goal.md plus 1–8 child taskN.md files; /stride-lite:create-task renders a single task markdown file; /stride-lite:init scaffolds a project-local .stride_lite.md with email plus three hook sections (## before_task, ## after_task, ## after_goal). The stride-lite-workflow skill is the file-based equivalent of the full Stride plugin's stride-workflow — it walks a goal directory through an eight-step task lifecycle (select → before_task → explore → implement → after_task → review → review-loop decision → completion + archive), dispatching the two read-only subagents at the right moments. Three subagents are shipped: stride-lite:create-decomposer (decomposes a free-text prompt into a goal + child tasks YAML, no API calls), stride-lite:task-explorer (read-only enrichment with codebase context — Read / Grep / Glob, no Bash, no WebFetch; appends ## Exploration Report), and stride-lite:task-reviewer (reviews changes against acceptance criteria, pitfalls, patterns, and testing strategy with narrowly-scoped read-only git Bash; appends ## Review Report with embedded reviewer_result JSON, schema 1.1). v0.9.0+: hooks/hooks.json registers Claude Code PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers that auto-fire the three .stride_lite.md sections at the corresponding workflow intercepts — ## before_task before the task-explorer Agent dispatch (blocking, exit 2 stops the dispatch), ## after_task before the task-reviewer Agent dispatch (blocking, exit 2 stops the dispatch), ## after_goal after the goal.md Edit/Write that appends ## Completion Summary (advisory — PostToolUse cannot roll back the write). Cross-platform from day one: hooks/stride-lite-hook.sh (POSIX bash, pure-bash JSON parsing, no jq dependency) and hooks/stride-lite-hook.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1+, ConvertFrom-Json / ConvertTo-Json, no module installs); the .sh script auto-delegates to .ps1 on native Windows (OSTYPE unset + COMSPEC set). v0.10.0+: stride-lite-workflow Step 8 final-task branch performs a terminal PENDING → IMPLEMENTED archive move — after ## after_goal fires, the goal directory moves from docs/implementation/PENDING/<slug>/ to docs/implementation/IMPLEMENTED/<slug>/ via git mv when tracked (preserves rename history) or plain mv otherwise. Collision suffixing on the target with -2 / -3 / … up to a 1000-iteration safety cap (never overwrites), after-goal-failure no-move guard (a structured failed-status JSON from the harness skips the move so the user can re-trigger), non-/PENDING/ path skip with a stderr warning (custom --output-dir is left where it is), and clean exit on filesystem-mv failure (logged, the workflow does not fail because of an archive-move failure). Single-task files under PENDING/tasks/ are NEVER moved — only goal directories. v0.11.0+: copy installs ship the hook enforcement layer — install.sh previously copied every directory except hooks/, so script-based installs silently lacked the documented auto-fire entirely (pre-0.11.0 copy installs should re-run ./install.sh --force); the installer now copies hooks/ with the executable bit preserved, reports it in the summary, and fails loudly if hooks.json does not land. Also: the init surface, workflow walkthrough, and scaffolded template all teach the v0.9.0 harness-executes model (the stale static-config and workflow-skill-executes claims are gone), phantom /stride-lite:ideate//stride-lite:decompose references are purged with the decomposer's unjustified Read/Grep grant removed, the smoke suite grows 24 to 43 assertions with machine-enforced init-template parity and nine hook-routing payload fixtures, and the shipped init-command goal artifact is archived PENDING to IMPLEMENTED per the plugin's own convention. v0.12.0+: three optional gated sub-steps in stride-lite-workflow, each dispatching an agent from a DIFFERENT plugin, all skipped cleanly when that plugin is absent and never able to fail a task — Step 6a maps a task's manual-test entries to charters and dispatches stride-exploratory-testing:explorer once per charter with a session budget read from the installed agent's own contract (the authorized-and-non-production affirmative is collected at Step 0 or never; it is never inferred from a localhost URL), Step 6b hardens confirmed findings into regression checks staged outside the test tree and never reported as passing since /harden holds no test runner, and Step 6c dispatches stride-security-review:security-reviewer in explicitly-declared considerations mode for one verdict per listed consideration, fail-closed so a consideration is never marked mitigated on a verdict set that could not be read. Also new: SECURITY.md states the trust boundary (the plugin executes arbitrary user-authored shell commands from .stride_lite.md, unvalidated and unwrapped) and records that the activation marker is a forgeable coordination signal and never an authorization, and that the PowerShell executor has not been verified on a real Windows host; dedicated hook test suites (hooks/test-stride-lite-hook.sh and .ps1) covering the section executor's internals; and Red flags plus Rationalization Table scaffolding across all four skills. Four defects fixed, three of them found by suites this release introduced: the PowerShell executor never received the hook payload at all, reading stdin via @($input) which is empty for the OS-level pipe the harness uses, so the documented auto-fire had never worked on native Windows and exited 0 without reporting it (D215); Start-Process -ArgumentList re-split every command so bash received only its first token, making every multi-word hook command silently do nothing while reporting success (D218); the decision matrix counted only table rows under ## Key files, so a hand-written bullet or numbered list of three real files resolved to skip-all with no explorer, no reviewer and no hooks, while the enrichment gate read the same section as populated (D216); and a three-backtick markdown fence wrapping a three-backtick json block closed early, rendering the rest of an agent contract as sample output — now caught by a fence walk in both backtick and tilde syntax, since neither a fence count nor an unterminated-fence check can see it (D217).

plugins.name: launchdarkly
plugins.description: Generate correct, testable, and removable LaunchDarkly feature-flag code from Claude Code — covers the Java server SDK and the TypeScript SDKs (Node server, client-side JS, React) with skills, scaffolding and flag-removal commands, and an anti-pattern review agent. v0.3.0+: the client-side skill is modernized to the scoped v4 SDKs (@launchdarkly/js-client-sdk and @launchdarkly/react-sdk with createLDReactProvider and typed hooks, the unscoped v3 packages preserved in a labeled legacy section); /launchdarkly:ld-scaffold gains real browser and react targets (four targets total); the reviewer agent gains eight-plus anti-pattern rules; and the plugin now ships a dependency-free scripts/smoke.sh validation gate.

plugins.name: stride-exploratory-testing
plugins.description: Drive structured, charter-based exploratory testing sessions in Claude Code — the discipline that supplies the "explored" half of Tested = Checked + Explored. Plan charters, run timeboxed sessions against a running app under an absolute safety boundary, judge results with oracles, and capture findings as an SBTM session sheet and debrief. Surface: six skills (stride-exploratory-testing orchestrator, chartering, heuristics, oracles, bug-advocacy, session), seven slash commands (/charter, /nightmare-headline, /explore, /pair, /recon, /debrief, /harden), and two subagents (charter-generator, explorer). Pairs with a human driving the app (/pair), turns confirmed bugs into drafted regression checks in your own test framework (/harden), and persists session artifacts, a charter backlog, and a coverage map under .exploratory/ so findings survive the conversation. Ships worked example fixtures (charter set, session sheet, debrief) and a pure-shell smoke-test harness under lib/. Encodes established exploratory-testing practice — Kaner, Hendrickson's Explore It!, SBTM (Bach), Whittaker's Tours, and Bach's Heuristic Test Strategy Model.
